description: Adversarial attack classes and defense mechanisms demonstrated by the Adversarial Face Recognition Lab.

attacks.name: Perturbation (Noise) Attack
attacks.description: Tiny imperceptible pixel noise flips the prediction.
attacks.mitigations: PGD adversarial training, input denoising, perturbation detectors.

attacks.name: Occlusion Attack
attacks.description: Blocking a critical region (eyes) removes the strongest identity features.
attacks.mitigations: Random erasing augmentation, attention regularization, partial-input checking.

attacks.name: Input Transformation
attacks.description: Photometric or geometric changes shift the model's confidence.
attacks.mitigations: Augmentation diversity, input normalization, distribution-shift detection.

attacks.name: Physical Attacks
attacks.description: Adversarial patches or patterns that fool models in the real world (beyond this lab's scope).
attacks.mitigations: Robust training, patch detectors, multi-view verification.

defenses.name: Adversarial Training
defenses.description: Train on adversarial examples to flatten the decision landscape.

defenses.name: Input Preprocessing
defenses.description: Denoise, normalize, and filter inputs before the model.
defenses.tradeoff: Can reduce legitimate signal if too aggressive.

defenses.name: Adversarial Detection
defenses.description: A guardrail that flags inputs that deviate from expected statistics.
defenses.tradeoff: Attacker can adapt to evade the detector.

defenses.name: Certified Defenses
defenses.description: Formally guaranteed robustness within a bounded perturbation.
defenses.tradeoff: Often lower clean accuracy and higher compute.
